aliases: Yangbajing High Altitude Cosmic Ray Laboratory

intervals.label: Tibet air-shower arrays operating
intervals.note: Start of the first (Tibet-I) array at Yangbajing; ARGO-YBJ joined in 2006. The facility's own founding date is not stated in the sources read.
intervals.quote: After three years of operation, starting in 1990, of the Tibet-I array

name: Yangbajing Cosmic Ray Observatory
notes: The facility name follows the abstract of the ARGO-YBJ detector paper ("YangBaJing Cosmic Ray Observatory"); the experiments also call it the Yangbajing Laboratory or Yangbajing High Altitude Cosmic Ray Laboratory.
No operator is recorded: the sources describe collaborations (ICRR and Chinese institutes; INFN and CAS) rather than a single operating body.

altitude.quote: Yangbajing (4300m above sea level, 90.53 deg E,30.11 deg N)

summary.plain: A Sino-Japanese and Sino-Italian high-altitude research site on the Tibetan plateau, 4300 metres above sea level, hosting air-shower arrays that study cosmic rays and gamma rays.
summary.technical: Yangbajing laboratory, 90 km north of Lhasa at 4300 m (606 g/cm2): home of the Tibet AS-gamma array (Tibet-I from 1990, Tibet-III from 1999) and ARGO-YBJ (2006-2013).
